approval.cost: No fee is stated anywhere in the official pages read
approval.trigger: Production access is gated by a mandatory review chain. Verbatim from the Introduction page: 'Production access is gated, and not all applications are approved. Production Pre-Approval is not a formality.' And: 'To launch on Gusto you must have an approved Production Pre-Approval and Security Review.' The developer journey has five phases (Onboard, Build, Review, Launch, Optimize); Production Pre-Approval runs alongside Onboard and Build, and approval is required before the Review phase can issue production keys. Information for the Security Review is collected inside the same Production Pre-Approval application. A quality review ('QA') and an approved Production Pre-Approval are required for ALL builds using the API before production keys are issued; for an Integrated App, the completed Partner Checklist is shared with Gusto for this review. Without approval, Gusto cannot provide implementation support, QA review, or production keys, and building before approval is explicitly at the developer's own risk because approval is not guaranteed. Scopes are assigned by Gusto during review based on the integration use case; they must be tested in the demo environment and are enforced in production, and any production call outside the assigned scope is rejected. Post-launch scope additions or changes go through Gusto developer support. Caps: none stated for demo applications/companies; sandbox keys simply cannot reach real customer data. Listing: no public marketplace/listing procedure for App Integrations was documented in the pages read beyond launch/promotion guidance.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration for Production Pre-Approval, Security Review, or QA review appears in the official pages read)

blockers.detail: Sandbox/demo keys (api.gusto-demo.com) cannot touch real customer data until Production Pre-Approval + Security Review + QA all pass and Gusto issues production keys. Approval is genuinely deniable: 'Production access is gated, and not all applications are approved', and Gusto warns that building first is at your own risk.
blockers.howToClear: Submit the Production Pre-Approval application as early as possible (Gusto explicitly recommends getting approval before building) and complete the Partner Checklist for QA.
blockers.title: Production is a hard gate, and approval can be denied

blockers.detail: Gusto assigns scopes during review from your use case; you do not pick them. Out-of-scope production calls are rejected, and changing scopes later is a support request, not a portal action.
blockers.howToClear: Specify the use case precisely in the pre-approval application and test the assigned scopes in the demo environment before launch.
blockers.title: You do not choose your scopes

blockers.detail: Refresh tokens never expire by time but are single-use: 'You may exchange your refresh token for a new access token once', and the refresh response returns a new refresh token. If your store does not atomically persist the newest refresh token (a crash mid-refresh, or two workers refreshing concurrently), silent renewal breaks and a human admin must re-authorize. Since the v2023-05-01 API version ('strict access'), an access token is also restricted to ONE company: a multi-company admin must complete OAuth separately for each company.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the returned refresh token atomically with the refresh call, serialize refreshes per company, and design a re-authorization path for when rotation state is lost.
blockers.title: Single-use refresh tokens and one-company tokens

flavor.recommended: An App Integrations application in the Gusto Developer Portal, using the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
flavor.why: The object is an application created in Gusto's Developer Portal (dev.gusto.com). Creating one requires a Developer Portal account plus completed Organization setup, and at least one redirect URI; Gusto generates a unique client_id and client_secret. Each customer company connects its own Gusto account through the authorization code flow, and the token received is scoped to that one company. There is no self-serve API-key model for third parties: the Introduction page states the Gusto API is currently restricted to Gusto App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners, and directs a Gusto customer who wants to connect their own company systems to use the Gusto CLI or Gusto MCP server instead of the API. Initial keys are for the sandbox/demo environment only (api.gusto-demo.com), with an auto-generated demo company (company info, employees, previous payrolls) for testing.

Missing or expired access tokens return 401; API calls use Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
No demo/test accounts are allowed in production after QA/launch, per the Introduction FAQ.

steps.detail: Create a Developer Portal account, complete Organization setup, and submit the Production Pre-Approval application as early as possible; the same application collects the Security Review information.
steps.title: Onboard; submit Production Pre-Approval early

steps.detail: Create the demo application with at least one redirect URI; record the client_id and client_secret. Use the auto-generated demo company (with employees and previous payrolls) at api.gusto-demo.com for testing.
steps.title: Create the demo application

steps.detail: GET api.gusto.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, and a random URL-safe state. The authorizing admin logs in and selects the company. On return, verify state matches, then POST api.gusto.com/oauth/token with a JSON body of client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code, grant_type=authorization_code. Store the access_token/refresh_token pair per company; call the API with Authorization: Bearer <access_token>.
steps.title: Build the authorization code flow

steps.detail: Refresh via the same token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, and atomically replace the stored refresh token with the new one returned (each refresh token is single-use).
steps.title: Refresh with rotation

steps.detail: If pre-approved, complete the Partner Checklist and share it with Gusto for the QA review. After approval, Gusto's Developer Relations team issues production keys.
steps.title: Complete QA (Partner Checklist); receive production keys

tagline: A partner-gated API where production is earned, not toggled: Production Pre-Approval, a Security Review, and a QA review all pass before Gusto issues production keys, and Gusto assigns your scopes for you. Refresh tokens never expire by time but die after a single use.
